title: Proverbs Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Proverbs chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Proverbs Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Proverbs Chapter 17.

questions.question: What is better according to Proverbs 17:1?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:1 states that a dry morsel with quietness is better than a house full of sacrifices with strife.

questions.question: Who shall have rule over a son that causeth shame?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:2 indicates that a wise servant shall have rule over a shameful son.

questions.question: What does the LORD try according to Proverbs 17:3?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:3 states that while the fining pot is for silver and the furnace for gold, the LORD trieth the hearts.

questions.question: A wicked doer giveth heed to what according to Proverbs 17:4?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:4 says that a wicked doer gives heed to false lips.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 17:5 states that he who mocks the poor reproaches his Maker.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:5 clearly states that whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 17:6, what are children's children to old men?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:6 says that children's children are the crown of old men.

questions.question: True or False: Excellent speech becometh a fool according to Proverbs 17:7.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:7 states that excellent speech does not becometh a fool, implying it is inappropriate.

questions.question: What is a gift compared to in Proverbs 17:8?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:8 compares a gift to a precious stone in the eyes of the one who has it.

questions.question: He that covereth a transgression seeketh what according to Proverbs 17:9?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:9 states that he that covereth a transgression seeketh love.

questions.question: True or False: A reproof enters more into a wise man than a hundred stripes into a fool according to Proverbs 17:10.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:10 indicates that a reproof has a greater impact on a wise man than harsh punishment does on a fool.

questions.question: In Proverbs 17, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: A wise servant shall have rule over a son
Better is a dry morsel and quietness
Children's children are the crown of old men
A reproof entereth more into a wise man
questions.correctAnswer: Better is a dry morsel and quietness
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:1 presents the first instruction in the chapter, emphasizing the value of quietness over abundance with strife.

questions.question: A friend loveth at all times, according to Proverbs 17:17. True or False?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:17 states that a friend loves at all times, affirming the loyalty of true friendship.

medium.title: Proverbs Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Proverbs Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 17:11 say about an evil man?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:11 states that 'An evil man seeketh only rebellion,' indicating that his intentions are consistently disruptive. This aligns with the theme of the consequences of wickedness found throughout Proverbs, such as in Proverbs 17:13, where rewarding evil for good leads to ongoing strife.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 17:14 describe the beginning of strife?
options: It is like letting out water.
questions.correctAnswer: It is like letting out water.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:14 compares the beginning of strife to 'when one letteth out water,' illustrating that just as water can be difficult to contain once released, so too can strife grow uncontrollable if not addressed promptly.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 17:12, who is more dangerous to meet: a bear robbed of her whelps or a fool in his folly?
options: A bear robbed of her whelps.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:12 suggests that encountering 'a fool in his folly' is more perilous than facing a bear deprived of her cubs, emphasizing the unpredictable and destructive nature of foolishness compared to a primal threat.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 17:16 imply about a fool's desire for wisdom?
options: A fool has no heart for wisdom.
A fool is wise in his own eyes.
questions.correctAnswer: A fool has no heart for wisdom.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:16 asks, 'Wherefore is there a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, seeing he hath no heart to it?' This indicates that a fool's lack of genuine desire for wisdom renders any effort to acquire it futile.

questions.question: True or False: According to Proverbs 17:20, a froward heart finds good.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:20 states, 'He that hath a froward heart findeth no good,' making it clear that a person with a twisted or perverse disposition will not find good results in their actions.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 17:17 characterize a true friend?
options: A friend is loyal in adversity.
questions.correctAnswer: A friend is loyal in adversity.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:17 declares, 'A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity,' highlighting that true friendship is steadfast, especially during hard times.

questions.question: What consequence does Proverbs 17:13 offer for rewarding evil for good?
options: Evil shall not depart from his house.
questions.correctAnswer: Evil shall not depart from his house.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:13 states, 'Whoso rewardeth evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house,' indicating that such actions will bring continual trouble and strife to the person's life.

questions.question: True or False: According to Proverbs 17:25, a foolish son brings joy to his father.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:25 states, 'A foolish son is a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bare him,' making it clear that a foolish child causes sorrow rather than joy.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 17:22 say a merry heart does?
options: It doeth good like a medicine.
questions.correctAnswer: It doeth good like a medicine.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:22 states, 'A merry heart doeth good like a medicine,' suggesting that joy and positive emotions can have healing effects, both mentally and physically.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 17:18, what does a man void of understanding do?
options: He striketh hands and becometh surety.
questions.correctAnswer: He striketh hands and becometh surety.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:18 indicates that a man lacking understanding engages in risky agreements, 'striketh hands' to become surety for another, which can lead to complications and regret.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 17:10 illustrate the difference in response to reproof between a wise man and a fool?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:10 states, 'A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool,' showing that a wise man values correction and learns from it, while a fool remains unyielding.

questions.question: What warning does Proverbs 17:19 provide about strife?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:19 states, 'He loveth transgression that loveth strife,' implying that those who pursue conflict and discord are courting their own destruction. It warns against engaging in strife.

hard.title: Proverbs Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Proverbs Chapter 17.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 17:21 say about the consequences of begetting a fool?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:21 states that 'He that begetteth a fool doeth it to his sorrow: and the father of a fool hath no joy,' indicating the emotional burden of raising a foolish child.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 17:22, what does a merry heart do?
options: It does good like a medicine
questions.correctAnswer: It does good like a medicine
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:22 says, 'A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones,' illustrating the healing power of a joyful disposition.

questions.question: Which of the following is a consequence of a wicked man taking a gift, as stated in Proverbs 17:23?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:23 states that 'A wicked man taketh a gift out of the bosom to pervert the ways of judgment,' highlighting the corrupting influence of bribery.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 17:24 suggest about the focus of a wise person compared to a fool?
options: Wisdom is before him that hath understanding
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom is before him that hath understanding
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:24 indicates that 'Wisdom is before him that hath understanding; but the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth,' emphasizing the wisdom of focusing on what is important.

questions.question: What is implied about a foolish son in Proverbs 17:25?
options: He brings joy to his father
He is a source of grief
questions.correctAnswer: He is a source of grief
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:25 states, 'A foolish son is a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bare him,' indicating the emotional pain caused by a foolish child.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 17:26, is it good to punish the just?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:26 states, 'Also to punish the just is not good, nor to strike princes for equity,' emphasizing the injustice of punishing the righteous.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 17:27 say about a person with knowledge?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:27 states, 'He that hath knowledge spareth his words: and a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit,' highlighting the wisdom in restraint.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 17:28 say about a fool who holds his peace?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:28 notes, 'Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding,' indicating that silence can be seen as wisdom.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 17:14 compares the beginning of strife to letting out water.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:14 states, 'The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with,' illustrating the destructive nature of strife.

questions.question: True or False: A friend is described in Proverbs 17:17 as someone who loves in times of adversity.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:17 states, 'A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity,' highlighting the loyalty of true friendship.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage connects to the theme of wisdom in Proverbs 17:24?
questions.explanation: James 1:5 encourages seeking wisdom from God, complementing Proverbs 17:24's emphasis on the importance of wisdom for those who understand.

questions.question: Which passage echoes the sentiment of not rejoicing in calamity found in Proverbs 17:5?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 24:17 advises against rejoicing when an enemy falls, echoing the warning in Proverbs 17:5 about not taking pleasure in calamities.

questions.question: In Proverbs 17:26, what is said about punishing the just?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:26 states that 'Also to punish the just is not good,' emphasizing the importance of justice for the righteous.

theological.title: Proverbs Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Proverbs Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 17:1 indicate is better than a house full of sacrifices?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:1 states that 'Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices with strife,' emphasizing the value of peace over abundance.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 17:3, what does the LORD do?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:3 says, 'but the LORD trieth the hearts,' indicating God's role in examining the true intentions and thoughts of humanity.

questions.question: What is said about a wise servant in Proverbs 17:2?
options: He will rule over a son that causeth shame
questions.correctAnswer: He will rule over a son that causeth shame
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:2 states, 'A wise servant shall have rule over a son that causeth shame,' showing that wisdom leads to honor and authority.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the heart from Proverbs 17:20?
options: A froward heart finds no good
questions.correctAnswer: A froward heart finds no good
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:20 states, 'He that hath a froward heart findeth no good,' illustrating the futility of a deceitful heart.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 17:9 teach about covering transgressions?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:9 states, 'He that covereth a transgression seeketh love,' indicating that forgiveness fosters relationships.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 17:15, who is an abomination to the LORD?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:15 declares, 'He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, even they both are abomination to the LORD,' emphasizing God's displeasure with injustice.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 17:24 suggest about the wise and the fool?
options: Wisdom is before him that hath understanding
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom is before him that hath understanding
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:24 states, 'Wisdom is before him that hath understanding; but the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth,' showing the accessibility of wisdom to those who seek it.

questions.question: In Proverbs 17:22, what is said to do good like medicine?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:22 states, 'A merry heart doeth good like a medicine,' highlighting the healing power of joy.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 17:14 indicate about strife?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:14 warns that 'The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with,' suggesting the importance of preventing conflict.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 17:12 compare encountering a fool in his folly to?
options: Meeting a bear robbed of her whelps
questions.correctAnswer: Meeting a bear robbed of her whelps
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:12 states, 'Let a bear robbed of her whelps meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly,' emphasizing the danger of folly.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 17:26 say about punishing the just?
options: It is a sign of justice
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:26 states, 'Also to punish the just is not good,' indicating that justice must be applied fairly.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 17:18 warn about a man void of understanding?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:18 indicates, 'A man void of understanding striketh hands, and becometh surety in the presence of his friend,' warning against foolish commitments.

questions.question: What principle can be drawn from Proverbs 17:5 about mocking the poor?
options: It is a sign of strength
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:5 states, 'Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker,' emphasizing the seriousness of mistreating the vulnerable.

questions.question: What is indicated about the father of a fool in Proverbs 17:21?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:21 states, 'He that begetteth a fool doeth it to his sorrow: and the father of a fool hath no joy,' indicating the pain of raising a foolish child.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 17:28 illustrate the wisdom of silence?
options: Even a fool is counted wise when silent
questions.correctAnswer: Even a fool is counted wise when silent
questions.explanation: Proverbs 17:28 states, 'Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding,' highlighting the value of discretion.
